2027-05-22.title: Saturday after the Sunday of Pentecost · St Rita
readings: “You are a letter of Christ... written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God”
The wise and foolish bridesmaids: “Keep awake therefore”
2027-05-22.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Sunday of Pentecost. The Panchangam remembers St Rita. This evening the First Sunday after Pentecost begins with Evening Prayer; its Evening Gospel is Luke 8:4–15.
2027-05-22.verse: you show that you are a letter of Christ, prepared by us, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.
theo: At the end of the first week of the season of Pentecost, St Paul gives us a picture of what the Holy Spirit does in a Christian. Some people in Corinth had begun to ask for Paul's credentials: where were his letters of recommendation? Paul answers: “Surely we do not need, as some do, letters of recommendation to you or from you, do we? You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts, to be known and read by all; and you show that you are a letter of Christ, prepared by us, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.” The tablets of stone recall Sinai, where God gave the Law to Moses; the Jewish people still keep the feast of Weeks, Shavuot, in memory of that gift, and it was on that very feast that the Spirit came upon the apostles. The prophets had promised a day when God would write his law within his people: “I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts” (Jeremiah 31:33). Paul says that day has come. The Spirit of Pentecost is a writer, and his paper is the human heart.

Paul goes on: “our competence is from God, who has made us competent to be ministers of a new covenant, not of letter but of spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.” This is not contempt for the Law, which Paul elsewhere calls “holy” (Romans 7:12), nor for the people to whom it was given. The Law shone with glory, so that the people “could not gaze at Moses' face because of the glory of his face.” But a commandment written outside us can only tell us what to do; it cannot give us the strength to do it. St Augustine put the difference simply: by the law of works God says, Do what I command; by the law of faith we say to God, Give what you command (On the Spirit and the Letter 13.22, in substance). The Spirit does not only show us the way; he becomes the life within us that walks in it. “How much more will the ministry of the Spirit come in glory?” The glory once seen on Moses' face is now meant to shine, quietly, in ordinary Christian lives, so that anyone who reads us reads Christ.

The Gospel tells us how to keep that letter legible: keep the lamp burning. Ten bridesmaids wait for the bridegroom; five take flasks of oil, five do not. “As the bridegroom was delayed, all of them became drowsy and slept.” Everyone sleeps; the difference is in the oil. When the cry comes at midnight, the foolish ask to borrow, and the wise cannot lend, because the oil of a life cannot be handed over at the last minute. St John Chrysostom saw in the oil the works of mercy, the kindness and almsgiving that keep faith burning (Homilies on Matthew 78, in substance). Today the Panchangam remembers St Rita of Cascia, a woman whose lamp burned through a long night. Born in Umbria about 1381, she was married young to a hard and violent man, and for years she answered him with patience and prayer; he changed, and then was murdered. She forgave his killers and prayed that her sons would not take revenge. After their death she entered the Augustinian monastery at Cascia, where she lived in prayer and penance until her death on 22 May 1457. Many in Kerala call on her as the patron of impossible causes. Her life was a letter written by the Spirit on a human heart, in a hand that anger and grief could not erase. Ask her prayers today for a marriage under strain, for a family divided by revenge, for a cause that looks hopeless, and keep your own lamp filled: “Keep awake therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour.”
outline: Ask: if someone read my life this week, what would they read about Christ?
Written by the Spirit on human hearts.
Not only the command, but the strength to keep it.
The wise bridesmaids and St Rita's long night of faith.
live: Choose one person at home or at work who finds faith hard, and let them read Christ in one concrete act of patience this week.
Do one work of mercy each day until next Saturday: a visit, an alms, a phone call to someone lonely.
2027-05-22.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, by your Holy Spirit you write your law on the tablets of our hearts and make us letters of your love for all to read. Write in us what you will. Do not let the letter of the law lie dead in us, but let your Spirit give us life and strength to do what you command. Keep our lamps filled with the oil of faith and good works, so that when you, the Bridegroom, come at midnight, we may go in with you to the wedding feast. By the prayers of St Rita, give patience to those who suffer at home, forgiveness to those who are wronged, and hope to those whose cause seems impossible. With your Father and your Holy Spirit, now and for ever. Amen.
altar: At the altar the Bridegroom comes to us now, before the midnight cry. In the Holy Qurbono he fills our lamps with his own life, so that we may burn until he comes.

quick: Paul: the Christians of Corinth are a letter of Christ, written by the Spirit of the living God on human hearts.
The letter kills, but the Spirit gives life: the Spirit gives the strength to do what God commands.
The wise bridesmaids kept oil for their lamps; St Rita's patient faith burned through a long night of suffering.
2027-05-22.action: Do one hidden work of mercy today to keep your lamp filled.
2027-05-22.question: What does my life say about Christ to those who read it?
kidsaint: St Rita and the rose in winter

Rita lived in Italy long ago. Her husband was often angry, but she was gentle and prayed for him, and he became kinder. Later she became a nun. An old story says that when she was dying in winter she asked for a rose from her garden, and her cousin found one blooming in the snow. That is why people give roses on her feast. Lesson: patience and prayer can make beautiful things grow even in hard times.

family.explain: Jesus told a story about ten girls waiting with lamps for a wedding. Five brought extra oil and five did not. The bridegroom came late at night, and the lamps of the five without oil were going out, so they missed the party. Jesus wants us to be ready for him always, with our lamps full: full of prayer and kindness every day, not only at the last minute.
family.intention: We pray for families who are going through hard times, and for anyone who feels their problem is impossible.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one way each of us can put oil in our lamp this week?”

illus: In a town in central Kerala a woman lived for many years with a husband who drank and shouted. Her neighbours told her to leave; her own brothers were ready to deal with him. Every Saturday she lit a candle before a small picture of St Rita and prayed the same prayer: give me patience, and give him a new heart. Her children grew up hearing her forgive. When her husband fell seriously ill, it was she who sat by him in the hospital. One night he asked a priest to hear his confession. Afterwards he said to her: all those years you were the only Bible I read. She did not tell anyone that for a long time; she said only that the candle had been worth it.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, by your Spirit you write on our hearts. Make our lives letters of your love, and keep our lamps burning. Amen.
share: You yourselves are our letter... to be known and read by all (2 Corinthians 3:2). What do people read in me?
The letter kills, but the Spirit gives life (2 Corinthians 3:6). Where do I need the Spirit's strength to do what I know is right?
Keep awake therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour (Matthew 25:13). Is my lamp ready?
pm.resp: Come, Holy Spirit, write on our hearts.
interc: For the Church, that her members may be letters of Christ read by all.
For couples whose marriage is under strain, that by the prayers of St Rita they may find patience, healing and peace.
For those who have been wronged, that they may have the grace to forgive and to refuse revenge.
For all who face impossible causes, that they may not lose hope.
For our parish as we begin the First Sunday after Pentecost, that our lamps may be full.
pm.close: Father, through your Spirit you write your law on our hearts and keep our lamps burning in the night. Make us faithful letters of your Son, give us the patience and forgiveness of St Rita, and keep us ready for the coming of the Bridegroom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul tells the Corinthians that he does not need letters of recommendation. You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts, to be known and read by all (2 Corinthians 3:2). They are a letter of Christ, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts (2 Corinthians 3:3). This is what Pentecost does: the Spirit writes God's law on our hearts.

For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life (2 Corinthians 3:6). A command written outside us tells us what to do; the Spirit within gives us the strength to do it. As St Augustine said (in substance), we can now pray: Lord, give what you command. The glory that shone on Moses' face is meant to shine quietly in our ordinary lives.

In the Gospel, ten bridesmaids wait for the bridegroom. All of them fall asleep; the difference is the oil. The foolish ask to borrow at the last moment, but the oil of a lifetime cannot be borrowed. Keep awake therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour (Matthew 25:13). Our oil is prayer and works of mercy, kept up day after day.

Today we remember St Rita, whose lamp burned through a long night: a hard marriage, the murder of her husband, the loss of her sons, and through it all patience, prayer and forgiveness. Let us ask her prayers for families in difficulty and for causes that seem impossible, and let us keep our lamps filled, so that our lives are letters in which others can read Christ. Amen.
kids: Children, St Paul says something surprising: you are a letter! Not a letter written with a pen, but a letter written by the Holy Spirit on your heart. When people see how you behave, kind or unkind, patient or angry, they are reading that letter. Today we remember St Rita, who stayed gentle and kept praying even when her life was very hard. Let's be letters that tell everyone how good Jesus is!

concl: The Spirit of Pentecost writes Christ on our hearts, so that our lives can be read by all.
Faith kept burning by prayer and mercy is the oil no one can lend us; St Rita kept hers through the longest night.
2027-05-22.resolve: Let the Spirit write on your heart, keep your lamp filled day by day, and be a letter in which others read Christ.
